answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks like an orchard grown from verified work: each newcomer locks a refundable deposit before transacting, then earns signed receipts by completing small verifiable tasks checked by randomly assigned peers. Every receipt is hash-chained to the previous one, so a fresh identity entering the meadow starts with no credit and must pay real work over time. The public ledger acts as a mirror — one forged receipt breaks the chain and exposes the whole cluster, slashing the deposit, so buying a pile of throwaway identities buys nothing.
